text:
juan: Hey team — after we migrated acct 3489 -> new-org, the customer saw a bunch of 429s for a ~30s spike even though they had burst credits. Can we check why burst credit cushioning didn't kick in?

erica: Oof. Any request IDs or example logs?

juan: Got a snippet from their app logs: 
```
POST /v1/generate 429
x-request-id: rq_8f3c
x-rate-limit-burst-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1670000210
```
They were at 95% of normal quota but expected the short spike to be covered by burst credits.

philip: Curious — migration might have recreated the billing/quotas mapping. Burst credits are stored on the quota bucket, not the org record. If bucket ID changed, remaining credits could be zero.

maria: @philip do we persist fractional burst credits? The customer claims they had "~1.8m token cushion" before cutover.

philip: Yes, we track credits as integer token units, plus a smoothing window state per bucket. However on migration we sometimes reset smoothing timers. That can make credits appear available but not usable until window warms up.

support-bot: Automated alert: customer acct 3489 reported 429 spike at 2530001205, region us-west1. Incident ID: INC-20253

juan: Is there a way to surface the smoothing window state and current credits in the admin panel for debugging? The customer is asking for proof.

erica: Not currently exposed, but we can query infra counters. @infra-bot can you pull the bucket-level credit ledger for bucket bkt_3489 for the timeframe?

infra-bot: Querying ledger... results: 
- pre-migration (2530000000): credits=1800000, smoothing_window_last_refill=2529999940
- post-migration (2530000100): credits=0, smoothing_window_last_refill=null, bucket_id changed -> bkt_9x2

juan: So it looks like the migration created a new bucket id and the credits didn't carry over. Customer saw zeros.

maria: That matches. We should: 1) restore credits to the new bucket, 2) add a one-off smoothing grace for the next 60s so their short spike doesn't hit 429s, 3) record a migration hook to transfer smoothing state.

philip: Agreed. For the immediate mitigation: we can top up bkt_9x2 by the missing tokens and set smoothing_window_last_refill to now-30s. I can run a patch.

juan: Can you paste the admin commands so I can share with customer?

philip: Run as infra-admin: 
```
POST /admin/buckets/bkt_9x2/credits
{ "delta": 1800000 }
PATCH /admin/buckets/bkt_9x2/meta
{ "smoothing_window_last_refill": 2530001400 }
```
Note: these endpoints are internal.

erica: I pushed the patch at 2530001300. Customer reports errors dropped immediately.

juan: They confirmed: "spike smoothed out, no more 429s after the patch" :tada:. Please follow up with a permanent fix.

maria: Action items: PH-2029 (ensure migration preserves bucket id or migrates credits), PH-2030 (admin UI telemetry to debug smoothing), and ops runbook update (temp top-up flow).

philip: One more gotcha to note for docs: when org->org migrations happen, batch backfills can exhaust the newly created bucket before smoothing warms up. Add a recommendation to do staged cutover with a pre-migration credit transfer.

juan: I'll send customer a summary and ETA for the migration fix. Thanks all.

maria: Nice catch, @juan. Also adding a line to support FAQs about "Why did I see a 429 despite burst credits?"

support-bot: Incident INC-20253 resolved (mitigated) at 2530001320.

juan: Closing thread, moving to follow-ups ticketed.
